Aptimizer Feature List  |  Page 2
Build Status: Where Aptimizer Stands Today
Aptimizer is built and running through V3. V1, V2 and V3 are functionally complete, and the V2.5 layer added
since the last feature list is complete apart from one item. V4 is roughly half built. V5, X and X+ are not built.
The headline figure: 324 of 420 catalogued features are built, with a further 28 partially built. Everything still
outstanding sits in enterprise workflow, BIM interoperability, and the long-range operating-system vision.
What was added since the previous feature list
The previous list catalogued 253 features across seven versions. This revision adds 167, almost all of them in a
new V2.5 band that did not exist before. The largest additions are:
 ■  Development controls and setbacks. Per-edge inward setbacks, setback minimums derived from plot area, the
height-driven open space table, and the height versus road width limit, with verification and warnings.
■  A real site layout engine. Buildable envelope generation, road network reservation with ring roads and internal
spines, amenity block placement, greedy grid tower packing with rotation sweep and spacing enforcement, and a
hard boundary containment guarantee.
■  Vastu and generative architecture. Sector mapping, sector-anchored unit packing, per-unit Vastu audit, MEP
position audit, and a measured plan realism check against a built reference drawing.
■  Programme and scheduling. Activity generation from quantities, full CPM with forward and backward passes,
critical path, float verification, work calendars, crew efficiency, prop removal safety rules, a target date solver, cash
flow, resource histogram and line of balance.
■  Development finance. Saleable area derivation, S-curve cost spread, monthly cash flow, NPV, IRR and
break-even.
■  Data reliability. Nine per-module data checks, freshness tracking, cross-module consistency checks, compliance
margin reporting and an overall trust score.
■  IS and NBC code intelligence. A 74-entry clause registry, clause text corpus indexing, semantic retrieval, and
verification of every clause the model cites against the real registry.
What is not built
 ■  Genetic refinement of tower placement. Placement is greedy grid packing only. The fitness function and GA
configuration exist; the refinement stage does not.
■  Approval workflow, comments and reviews, and workflow automation in V4.
■  All BIM interoperability in V5. There is no IFC, DWG, DXF, Revit or AutoCAD export.
■  Digital twin, IoT and construction monitoring in V5.
■  The Aptimizer X operating system layer. Several X features exist in partial form because a V2.5 or V3 module
already covers part of the ground, but none is complete at X scope.
Stated plainly: Aptimizer is a complete V3 product with a substantial V2.5 precision layer on top, partial V4
collaboration, and no V5 or X capability yet.

Cutting across every stage
Two capabilities do not sit at a single point in the workflow, which is why they do not appear as a stage of their
own.
 ■  AI assistance (V3). APT, the optimisers and the AI advisors are reachable from every module, and each draws on
the values that module has already computed. The assistant is context-aware by stage rather than being a separate
destination.
■  Data reliability (V2.5). The checks run continuously against every module, but the report is placed in Deliver on
purpose. The question it answers is whether the drawing set can be issued, and that is worth asking immediately
before the report is generated, not while the design is still moving.
Reading order note: a stage is only as trustworthy as the stage before it. Setbacks decide the buildable
envelope, the envelope decides tower placement, placement decides areas, areas decide quantities, quantities
decide cost and programme. An error at stage 1 propagates through all five, which is the reason the data
reliability checks exist at all.
